quest.title: Revelation Beneath the Stars
quest.description: Why do people start to forget Durin? You and Paimon have no clue. Just then, the magic book offers another hint — M's story does not end in Simulanka. And the next chapter seems to lead to where Durin first set foot in this world...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jean!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Hello, you two! I'm glad you got my letter. Durin's awake and waiting on the bench over there. I'm here if you need help. Just give me a shout.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about us! We'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Oh, hey you two. Ugh, I just remembered what happened right before I passed out. Thanks for holding me back... I shudder to think what might have happened if you hadn't.

choices.text: Don't worry about that for now.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I'm fine now, it's just... a lot of people seem to have forgotten me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we'll figure out a way to fix this. Why don't you start by telling us what happened?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It felt... so strange...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: After I realized no one recognized me anymore, I suddenly felt like I'd completely lost contact with my body.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Abyssal power lies sealed within this body I inhabit, so when I lost my connection to it, I lost control of that power too...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It wasn't until I heard everyone calling my name that I was able to reconnect with my body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You... lost contact with your body? Does that mean there's something wrong with it? Sounds like we need Albedo more than ever...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...I don't think the problem lies in Albedo's alchemy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... But, then, why are people forgetting you? Guess that's what we need to figure out...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think it's got something to do with that book.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means we need Alice for sure... But it's been ages and she still hasn't been in contact...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Now would be a really good time for a hint...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: How could the story's budding branches even hope to reach beyond the towering walls?

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Leaving the castle, the witch went off in search of the tallest, grandest tree in the whole world.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: High up in the canopy of that tree she sought a resting place, a refuge where the little sapling might take root.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Go to that place, for it was there that the sapling felt its first breath of wind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Was that another clue...? Does that mean the story isn't over yet?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Leaving the castle...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It just occurred to me — if this story is all about my own experiences, then wouldn't what happened after I left Simulanka be part of it too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But... how could she possibly know exactly what would happen? And even if she did, how could WE know when the story was complete?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like we gotta go back inside the book.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Since we can't reach Alice right now, we'll just have to get to the bottom of this ourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But first, we gotta figure out where this riddle wants us to go.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The tallest, grandest tree in the whole wide world, huh... The only place that ever gave me that feeling was the one I ended up in right after leaving Simulanka.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: They had great coffee there too, and so many books you'd never run out of things to read!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mean... Sumeru City?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Think about it — our search in Mondstadt began in a library, right? Well, Sumeru City's got one of those too, and it's absolutely huge! Whaddaya say, shall we try looking there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that does kinda make sense. And, it's not like Paimon's got a better idea.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's worth a shot, at least.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! Let's just give Jean and the others a heads-up first.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Well, it sounds like you've got a plan, so I won't interfere.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: All I ask is that you stay safe. Albedo won't be back for some time, and until he is, we can't know for sure how dangerous Durin might be in his current state.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I'm... I'm so sorry about what happened before.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Believe me, I'm not blaming you, and neither is anyone else here. If anything, it's the opposite — we're all just worried about you.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Worried... about me?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Come with me. I want to show you something.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: As soon as they heard you were awake, they all hurried over to see how you were doing.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Y—You all... came to see me?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: A little birdie told me you're working on finishing a storybook. So, maybe all those people losing their memories is just a... plot twist waiting to be resolved.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Miss Lisa! You... always seem to know how to put my mind at ease.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Please, everyone, don't worry about me! When I get back, I'll find a way to complete my mother's story, and the one we started too!

choices.text: Are you alright?

talks.objective: Head to the House of Daena with Durin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After the library hunt in Mondstadt, it's not as if Paimon was expecting this to be easy. But this... Yeah, this is something else.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Where do we even begin?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even the clue this time seemed kinda cryptic.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's just... take a look around?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Guess the best we can do is stay on the lookout for more weird things going on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Sorry, what was that?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm here to return volume five.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: According to the catalog, volume five of this series is not available for loan. I can't accept the return of a book that was never checked out in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Then let me put it this way: my copy is complete. Yours, on the other hand, is missing large amounts of content — so you should swap it for mine instead.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Sir, you have to understand... managing a library is a serious business and we have protocols in place for this kind of thing. I can't just replace an important volume in our collection based on nothing more than your word.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look what the wandering tom dragged in!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you.

choices.text: Well well, what a surprise...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And, uh, what is it you're doing here?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'm a traveling scholar, as you know. Isn't a library the most natural place for me to be?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, the last time we saw you was all the way in Nod-Krai. Paimon just didn't expect to suddenly see you in Sumeru, that's all...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: There were some things I needed to come back and take care of. Some documents had gone missing, so I tracked them down, restored them to their original condition, and now, I'm here to return them.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: And considering what I'm planning to do next, it feels like a weight off my shoulders...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: What's going on with you, huh? You look like a kicked puppy.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hat Guy... Ah, at least you haven't forgotten about me.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: What's that supposed to mean?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: #Durin fills {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]} in on recent events.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: So it's been getting worse...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like you know something we don't?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: After he left Simulanka, he spent some time traveling Sumeru with me.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I was working on several texts at the time, and I stumbled upon something strange.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Any time "Durin of Simulanka" was mentioned, before long, the record would disappear.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Which means, all the remaining records on "Durin" are about the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How did you even discover that?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: If I remember correctly, Hat Guy loved the time he spent in Simulanka so much that he started writing a travelogue.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That's besides the point. The fact is, you're not affected by the Ley Lines of this world. I'm sure you can grasp the implications of what that means.

choices.text: Irminsul...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: His case is different from mine. It's more like the world itself refuses to accept his existence.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It started with a few written records. But now, it sounds like it's spread to people who never met him, or didn't know him well. At this rate, the whole world might forget him altogether.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The whole world? But that includes all my friends in Mondstadt, and even Hat Guy too...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So that's what you've been worried about, all this time? Why didn't you just tell me?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: There are more important questions right now. Like, figuring out how to fix this.

choices.text: Yeah, we've been trying for a while now.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: That mage clearly cared a lot about her child. She left that book behind for a reason. If you want answers, isn't that the place to find them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think that didn't occur to us already? Problem is, we need to find the memory that unlocks the next chapter first.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmm... Mind if I take a look?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're offering to help us?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I just want to know what secrets this book is hiding. Besides, I've run into a bit of... "red tape", so I've got time.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Of course, be my guest!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the memory we've been looking for was about you, all along...

choices.text: We just haven't got to the bottom of it yet.
The things you've done...
I had a sneaking suspicion we'd see you here.

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the world where this chapter takes place? Looks like we're at the top of some kind of gigantic tree.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The story just now...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: This one must be about what happened to me when I first arrived in Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: No wonder the memory that unlocked it was about Hat Guy... Most of my memories from that period were.
Hold on, anyone wanna explain how I ended up looking like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft...!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Maybe you've become a character in the story too?

choices.text: The way you appear here...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You see me as... a stray cat!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A wandering tom, to be exact! Hehe, you should count yourself lucky! Of all Durin's friends, your character is by far the most... memorable.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Maybe it's because I've known Hat Guy for longer, so my impression of him is... more vivid than the others?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Vivid!? Then how come you haven't changed one bit!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Guess that means the impression {NICKNAME} left was so vivid it didn't need changing, hehe...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmph...

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Hello, everyone! Ready for today's adventure?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's the storybook Durin...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Oh? So you're not playing yourself in this one?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Does that mean, the two of you have even more "memorable" roles to play?

choices.text: This is Alice's magic we're talking about here...

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Where are we going today, kitty cat?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Ugh, whatever. Just follow me, same as always.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Okie-dokie! Can we chat along the way?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: If you have something to say, just say it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was that... seriously how the two of you communicated when you first got here...?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yep!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Anyway, how do we get ourselves out of here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Usually, the narrator gives hints to help us figure out what to do. Ahem, speaking of which... About time we got some of those, don'cha think?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The story's vines had woven themselves together into a giant tree, the boughs of which a little storyless dragon now paced, homeless among its leaves.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: He had to find a way to leave this place and set off in search of a home of his own. If he stayed, the world would erase him from its memory altogether.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: To leave this place? But... where am I supposed to go?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The little dragon felt completely lost. Just like the vines, the road ahead branched off into different directions, twisting and turning before disappearing into the mist.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: But as luck would have it, a prophetess waited up ahead. Perhaps she might know where each path might take him...

choices.text: She's the only one who can make sense of it.
...Is basically how Durin sees you.

dialogues.text: You must be the little lost dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: It's true... My friends and I are lost.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: This meeting was no accident. The "prophetess" was in fact the seer-witch, here to present her promised gift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The seer-witch... Ohhh yeah, that's Mona's teacher, right? The "old hag"?

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: Insolent child! I am the seer-witch, your prophetess — not some old hag!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Sorry!

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: Now, little lost dragon, I have come to bestow the gift I once promised — a prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: A prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: Hear me now, for my prophecy is this: one day, the dragon from beyond the castle shall be reborn, and none may avert its coming.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The wind took the prophecy and swept it off into the distance, and so the little dragon was shown a path to wander.

choices.text: A path shown by the wind...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: As far as I remember, once that alchemist from Mondstadt learned about the prophecy, he chose to stand with you against the evil dragon.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: So, what does any of this have to do with you being forgotten?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem... O wise witch of prophecy, could we trouble you with another question?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: As enigmatic as she was elegant, the seer-witch spoke no more — for her thoughts had long since returned to the starry firmament above.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, just when we actually needed her...

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: The seer-witch was my mother's friend, so the prophecy she just gave should turn out to be helpful.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Well, it's not like we've got better options... But, if all we need to do is leave this place, which path should we take?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Any ideas, Durin?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Why don't we take a look around?

choices.text: Could that be referring to what happened back in Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we go this way, we'll be heading back to Mondstadt, just like we planned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Out of all the options so far, this seems like the safest, right? At least we know what happens next...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He helps stop the evil dragon from returning, gets a new body, makes a whole bunch of friends...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Who all just... forget about him.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But... You didn't forget, Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm just saying, choosing this path wouldn't solve the main problem. You'd still end up being forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Huh...

choices.text: Maybe future chapters hold the answers.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'm not against choosing this path. I just wonder what secrets it might be hiding.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Let me think about it...

choices.text: We just need to keep the story going.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Returning to the castle...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh, well that's an interesting thought. Has the idea of returning to Simulanka ever crossed your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Returning to Simulanka...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Think about it, it's a place where a heartfelt wish is all it takes to rewrite the cruelest fate... Not like here, where fate mocks us all.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If there really is a being controlling the fate of this world, it must be a laughably spiteful creature, deaf to the wishes of others.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If you leave this world and its cruel fate behind, maybe your problems will be solved.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't give him crazy ideas like that!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I was simply expressing my envy, that's all. Not everyone is lucky enough to have a place like Simulanka to return to.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Well... let's say that you did. Would you choose to go back?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Of course not. I'd rather show fate who's boss instead.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you think, Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just... need some time to think this over.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: It seemed to lead away from this place, but each time he tried to follow it, the branches of the tale sent him back to the start.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh, so the author managed to work this book into the story, too. I'll hand it to her, this book is fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What's going on here...?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: When I first realized you were being forgotten by the world, I thought it might be because you'd spent too much time with me.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: In which case, the only hope of a cure... would be to cut our ties for good.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What makes you think that?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Once upon a time, the stray tore apart his own story and was forgotten by the world beyond the castle.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: He believed the story had cursed him, and that his misfortune had rubbed off upon the little dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: The story's curse...

choices.text: (So he thought, the fact that he was forgotten...)

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It was just a suspicion before, but now I think it's something we have to try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what do you mean? Try what?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: One of the story's branches is a path I can't take. If you follow it out of here, I won't be part of your story anymore.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Considering what the strange magic in this book is capable of, making that choice could cut our connection once and for all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not this again...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: As long as there's a chance it might work, it's worth a try.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: He's not like me. He deserves for the world to remember him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you think, Durin?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Well... maybe Hat Guy has his reasons for thinking that way, but that's not the kind of decision I can make so easily.

choices.text: (Affected Durin too...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we go this way, we'll be returning to the castle.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Returning to the castle...

choices.text: There's nothing challenging for you back there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You'll just be hiding from your problems and pretending like none of this ever happened. Is that really what you want, Durin?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...I see.

choices.text: You'll end up stuck in one place.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: It seemed to lead away from this place, but each time he tried to follow it, the branches of the tale sent him back to the start.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh, so the author managed to work this book into the story, too. I'll hand it to her, this book is fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we go this way, Durin will forget about you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You'd be choosing a branch of the story that I can't take... Paimon might be right about that.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But, at the same time, it could be the answer to your problem. It's worth a shot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That won't solve anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're one of Durin's best friends. His memories of you are extremely important to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What Paimon's trying to say is... If Durin forgets you, he'll never be able to complete his story.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Fair enough. I guess we'll just have to keep searching.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, that last ending was awful... No way we're picking that path again!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What are you even talking about? Hurry up and pick a path so we can get out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Let's pick one together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like the others aren't aware of what just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon's not sure how we'd even explain it... Guess all we can do is warn them if they're about to choose wrong again.

talks.objective: Go toward where the wind is coming from

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the world beyond the castle, no paper boat had ever flown before.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hey, if our goal is to just leave this place, what's stopping us from riding it out of here?

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: But... paper boats can't fly in the world outside the castle, silly...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You really think it'll fly?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Well, we can give it a try, can't we?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: When I first left Simulanka, I encountered all sorts of difficulties.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: And it was mainly because, just like the other characters in the storybook world, I only knew how to handle things the way the story said to.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But actually, the real world is full of endless possibilities. And if I'd thought about it differently, I'd have realized none of those "difficulties" existed in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What I'm trying to say is, who says we can't make paper boats fly, even in the world beyond the story? We just have to find a way.

choices.text: Let's give it a shot.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Okay! Let's do it!

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Finally, the little dragon and his friends decided to climb aboard the paper boat...

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: ...And to their wonder, it really did take flight.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Whoa! So it really can fly, after all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, we should've just tried that earlier...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: C'mon, it's time to leave this place.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Carried by the wind, the boat took flight, bound for the place foretold by the prophecy.

choices.text: Anything is possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on... That looks familiar!

choices.text: Wait, isn't that...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yep, that's The Durin alright.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, what's it doing here?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Beside the story's branches, there appeared... an origami boat from another tale.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Judging from the narrator's reaction, it probably wasn't meant to be part of this chapter.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: This was the exact boat that Hat Guy and I rode when we set off to explore Teyvat...

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Wow, so we can actually ride it?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Of course, and it can even fly! Back in Simulanka, me and my friends used to be able to hop on and get almost anywhere in no time.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Whenever I'm lost in Teyvat, I can't help thinking about it. Imagine how great it would be if they had something like this there too...

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: So did the little dragon become enraptured by this fantasy — and fantasy it was, for in the world beyond the castle, no paper boat had ever flown before.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Oh, yeah... How could a paper boat even fly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Way to kill the mood, narrator.

choices.text: The Durin?

talks.objective: The story will eventually reach its conclusion...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As the little dragon slipped back inside the castle's walls, the clamor of the outside world fell away.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: There was no danger here, no problems for the little dragon to resolve.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As soon as his mother finished her story, it was time for the child to drift off into the world of dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the story ended — with the little dragon fast asleep in his castle, just like he had never even hatched.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What's going on? I feel so weak...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's happening? Durin, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've reached an ending...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, but... this can't be how it ends! Durin promised to bring back everyone's memories... There's no way he'd accept an ending like this!

talks.objective: Walk the path where the stray cat cannot go...
The prophecy is destined to come true...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon left along the path his companion could not take — and from that point forth, the stray was no longer part of his story.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet his memories of the stray were an indispensable part of his tale.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: With the stray gone, the story lost the very spark that had first set it in motion.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the end, the little dragon's story faded into nothingness — and in the world beyond the castle, only the evil dragon's tale endured.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Who... am I?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Is this... me?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the story ended — with the little dragon fading from sight, leaving nothing but the evil dragon's shadow in his place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... the story ended?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, but Durin... Ugh, way to go, Hat Guy!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As enigmatic as she was elegant, the seer-witch spoke no more — for her thoughts had long since returned to the starry firmament above.

talks.objective: Discuss your experience within the story with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that was the "secret"...?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh...

choices.text: I see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, but... What does that mean?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You still don't get it? Simulanka Durin and Teyvat Durin share a special kind of connection: their fates are mirror images of one another.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: While they were in two separate worlds, there may have been some mutual influence, but their fates were independent.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: But when Simulanka Durin came to Teyvat, a version of his fate already existed there. So, how can two fates exist at the same time?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: The answer is, they can't. The rules of this world don't allow it. You can't return a book you never checked out in the first place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, so... what's Durin supposed to do?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmph, those mages seem to have come up with quite the ingenious solution...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'm here to make a return.

response.speaker: Katayoun
response.text: As I said, there's no record of volume five of this series ever being checked out.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Then just think of this as volume six. Based on what I know, the author was planning on publishing another volume, anyway.

response.speaker: Katayoun
response.text: Hmm, the catalog does have a slot reserved for volume six. So... this is it?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Sure, let's go with that. All you need to know is, I'll be the one writing this series from now on.

response.speaker: Katayoun
response.text: You... *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you up to this time...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Remember the "red tape" I mentioned before? Well, I just took care of it. Now, I guess you'll be off to see your alchemist friend?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It should be pretty obvious by now, he has the answers you're looking for.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we do have a whole bunch of things to confirm with Albedo, that's for sure. But didn't Jean say he'd be gone for quite a while?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'll join you. Just let me know when it's time to go.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hat Guy...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Don't sound so surprised. I'm part of this story too, aren't I? I'm just... playing my role.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Well, yeah... but it's not that. I just feel like... you want to help, but something's holding you back.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: When I first realized you were being forgotten by the world, I thought it might be because you'd spent too much time with me. I even thought cutting our ties might be the only way to fix it.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Why would you think that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (He once made the whole world forget him, so he was worried Durin might be affected by what he did...)

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It doesn't matter now. Judging from the answer this book has given us, I was probably overthinking it.

choices.text: Make that "definitely."

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Just as well. With the Ley Lines rejecting him like this, the people who still remember him are his only remaining connection to this place.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: If that last fragile tie was broken, who can say what devastation his unbound body might unleash?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: And to think I'm one of the people keeping you here, instrumental in helping change your fate... Huh, can't say I saw it coming.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Well, if it's good enough for Hat Guy, it's good enough for me... After all, he is about as odd as humans get.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Excuse me?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: With some people, even if you try asking a simple question, they'll always give you a complicated answer — and the more you ask, the more complicated it gets. Truth is, Hat Guy's just that kinda guy.

choices.text: Sometimes, for sure...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Whatever. All I needed was a yes or no, so we can quit it with all the back and forth.

choices.text: But he isn't always like that.
Anyway, we're in this together now.
I'm confused...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the world beyond the castle, no paper boat had ever flown before.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Unless the little dragon kept moving, eventually, he would be forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Beyond the story's branches lay only emptiness, a realm where none may tread.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Looking back the way he had come, the little dragon saw a gentle glow — a warm light that reminded him of somewhere familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The castle his mother had built for him still stood tall as ever, and in the paradise behind its walls lingered many joys of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Its gates were always open for him, a haven where no tales of wicked dragons were told.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You really wanna return to the castle, don't you, little dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: When you're there, no problem ever feels too big for you to solve...

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Yeah, I guess I do feel that way sometimes...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh? Looks like there's another path over here.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The secrets he sought led the stray to discover another path forward, though it was overgrown with bristling thorns.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Go to that place, for it was there that the sapling felt its first breath of wind.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The wind took the prophecy and swept it off into the distance, and so the little dragon was shown a path to wander.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The story will eventually reach its conclusion...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The prophecy is destined to come true...
